A river that changed course
A hurricane and heavy rain
41.e: Bão đổ bộ vào bờ biển và mưa lớn gây lũ.

41.q: Why did the volunteers carry packages on foot?
o: They did not have any cars or trucks to use.
It was faster than driving through the villages.
The charity wanted them to exercise.
Roads were blocked by mud, fallen trees and rocks.
41.e: Đường bị chặn nên phải mang hàng bộ qua những lối nhỏ.

41.q: What did the woman who had lost almost everything do?
o: She asked the volunteers for money and clothes.
She guarded the supplies.
She shared her rice with the volunteers.
She left the village.
41.e: Người phụ nữ mất gần hết vẫn nhất quyết chia cơm cho các tình nguyện viên.

41.q: What did the team leader advise?
o: Do not talk to the victims about their loss.
Try to solve every problem.
Work faster.
Just listen and do whatever you can.

41.q: What did the writer believe before volunteering?
o: That charities waste money
That floods are not really dangerous for local people
That villagers are unfriendly
That helping is only for rich or powerful people
41.e: Trước đây tác giả nghĩ giúp đỡ là việc của người giàu hoặc người có quyền lực.

41.q: Before this, the writer had volunteered in many disasters.
41.e: Tác giả chưa từng làm việc nào như vậy.

41.q: Helicopters dropped food and fuel to places the volunteers could not reach.
41.e: Trực thăng thả thức ăn và nhiên liệu đến những nơi không đi bộ tới được.

41.q: The writer found the mental effort harder than the physical work.
41.e: Công việc nặng nhọc về thể chất, nhưng nỗ lực tinh thần còn khó hơn.

41.q: The writer was injured during the work.
41.e: Bài chỉ nói tác giả trở về kiệt sức; không nói bị thương.

41.q: Would you like to volunteer in a difficult situation like this? What could you offer, and what would be hardest for you?
41.h: Dùng "I would…" để nói điều bạn sẵn sàng làm và kỹ năng có thể đóng góp, rồi "The hardest thing for me would be…" kèm lý do.

42.q: What made the writer change his lifestyle?
o: He lost his job.
He failed a fitness test at the gym near his office.
His friend got sick.
The doctor warned him about stress and bad habits.
42.e: Bác sĩ cảnh báo cơ thể đang phản ứng với căng thẳng và thói quen xấu.

42.q: What breathing technique did the writer learn?
o: Breathe quickly through the mouth whenever you start to feel nervous.
Hold your breath as long as possible.
Breathe in through the nose, hold for four seconds, breathe out slowly.
Breathe only when exercising.
42.e: Kỹ thuật thở được mô tả từng bước.

42.q: How does the writer cook now instead of frying?
o: He eats only raw food.
He uses more oil.
He bakes or boils.
He buys ready meals.
42.e: Thay vì chiên, tác giả nướng hoặc luộc.

42.q: Why did the writer reduce his drinking?
o: His doctor banned it.
Alcohol was too expensive for him at the weekend.
Alcohol made his mood worse the next day.
His gym did not allow it.
42.e: Rượu làm tâm trạng tệ hơn vào ngày hôm sau.

42.q: What does "Listen to it while it is still whispering" mean?
o: Notice small warning signs early, before problems become serious.
Speak quietly to your body when you feel any pain in it.
Go to the doctor every week, even when you feel completely well.
Ignore small pains.
42.e: Ẩn dụ: hãy chú ý những dấu hiệu nhỏ trước khi cơ thể buộc ta phải thay đổi.

42.q: The doctor found a serious illness.
42.e: Bác sĩ không thấy gì nghiêm trọng nhưng đưa ra lời cảnh báo.

42.q: The writer started building muscle slowly with a trainer.
42.e: Tác giả tập gym và tăng cơ từ từ với huấn luyện viên.

42.q: The writer started a journal to write down his emotions.
42.e: Tác giả bắt đầu viết nhật ký cảm xúc.

42.q: The writer changed his job to reduce stress.
42.e: Bài không nói tác giả đổi việc.

42.q: Which of your daily habits is good for your body and mind, and which one would you like to change? Explain how.
42.h: Nêu một thói quen tốt và một thói quen muốn bỏ; dùng "Instead of + V-ing, I will…" để mô tả cách thay đổi.

43.q: Why was the writer unhappy in her marketing job?
o: The company was failing.
Her manager did not respect her.
Her real passion was teaching.
The salary was too low.
43.e: Lương tốt, công ty uy tín, nhưng đam mê thật sự của tác giả là dạy học.

43.q: How did the writer prepare for the career change?
o: She quit her job immediately and started applying to schools.
She moved to another country.
She asked her parents for money to pay for a course.
She researched teaching, took an evening course and volunteered.
43.e: Tác giả lên kế hoạch kỹ thay vì hành động ngay.

43.q: Why did the writer volunteer at a community centre on Saturdays?
o: Because her course required it
To gain experience and check whether she enjoyed teaching
To meet new friends
To earn extra money at the weekends for her course
43.e: Mục đích được nêu bằng to-V.

43.q: What did the head teacher think of the writer's business background?
o: It was too short.
It was more important than her teaching qualifications.
It was not useful for teaching young students at all.
It gave a fresh impression of what a teacher could be.
43.e: Hiệu trưởng ấn tượng và thấy kinh nghiệm kinh doanh mang lại góc nhìn mới về người giáo viên.

43.q: In the last paragraph, "do not jump without a plan" means …
o: do not make a big change without preparing
do not leave your job ever
do not do any sport without a coach to help you
do not move to a new house
43.e: Ẩn dụ "nhảy": đừng thay đổi lớn khi chưa có kế hoạch.

43.q: The writer worked in marketing for eight years.
43.e: Tác giả làm marketing tám năm.

43.q: The writer's parents were worried about financial security.
43.e: Bố mẹ lo lắng về an toàn tài chính.

43.q: The writer earns more money as a teacher than before.
43.e: Tác giả kiếm ít hơn và đóng thuế nhiều hơn mình tưởng.

43.q: The writer teaches English at the secondary school.
43.e: Bài không nói tác giả dạy môn gì.

43.q: Would you change your career or field of study if you were not happy? What would you need to do before making the change?
43.h: Dùng câu điều kiện loại 2 (If I were not happy, I would…), rồi liệt kê 2–3 bước chuẩn bị (First, I would research… / Then…).

44.q: How did the writer feel about history at school?
o: It was too easy.
It was exciting and full of stories about real people.
It was her favourite subject.
It was boring, just dates and names to remember.
44.e: Ở trường, lịch sử chỉ là danh sách ngày tháng, vua chúa và trận đánh phải học thuộc.

44.q: Why did the writer feel sympathy for the princess?
o: She had no freedom despite her wealth.
She was poor and had to work in the palace.
She had no family.
She died young in a battle.
44.e: Công chúa giàu có nhưng không có tự do (bị gả năm 15 tuổi).

44.q: What was special about the ancient port?
o: It was the biggest and busiest port in the world.
It was built by the prince.
It was destroyed by a storm.
Different religions existed side by side there.
44.e: Đền, nhà thờ và thánh đường Hồi giáo ở cùng một con phố.

44.q: What did the old man in the village say we must remember?
o: The names of all the soldiers who died
Not to hate, but to understand
To build more graves
To hate our enemies

44.q: According to the writer, what is history really about?
o: Ordinary people who loved, suffered and hoped
Wars and battles
Famous leaders and the decisions they made
Kings and royal families
44.e: Lịch sử không chỉ là về những nhà lãnh đạo nổi tiếng.

44.q: The princess was married at fifteen to a man she had never met.
44.e: Công chúa lấy chồng năm mười lăm tuổi với người chưa từng gặp.

44.q: Sailors traded silk, cotton, spices and gold at the ancient port.
44.e: Thủy thủ đông và tây gặp nhau ở đó để buôn tơ lụa, bông, gia vị và vàng.

44.q: The old man in the village had fought in the battle himself.
44.e: Trận đánh xảy ra khi ông còn nhỏ; ông chỉ cho xem mộ những người lính.

44.q: The writer now works as a history teacher.
44.e: Bài không nói tác giả làm nghề gì.

44.q: Describe a historical place you have visited or would like to visit. What can it teach us about the people who lived there?
44.h: Mô tả địa điểm (It is located… / It was built…), một chi tiết ấn tượng, và bài học về con người thời đó (It shows that…).

45.q: How did following the news so closely affect the writer?
o: He became well informed and much calmer than before.
He became anxious, angry and tired.
He became a journalist.
He stopped voting.
45.e: Tác giả tưởng mình hiểu biết nhưng thực ra lo âu, tức giận và mệt mỏi.

45.q: According to the uncle, why do we see more violent stories than good ones?
o: Journalists prefer sad stories.
Good news is illegal.
Bad news attracts attention, and the press needs viewers.
Violent things happen more often than good things.
45.e: Báo chí cần người xem, và tin xấu thu hút sự chú ý.

45.q: What should you do before you believe a story?
o: Watch a documentary about it.
Read the comments under the article to see what other people think.
Check whether official or independent sources confirm it.
Share it with friends.
45.e: Kiểm tra xem nguồn chính thức, nhà báo độc lập hoặc tòa án có xác nhận không.

45.q: According to the text, what might a headline that makes you extremely angry be designed to do?
o: Entertain you
Influence you
Educate you
Inform you
45.e: Tiêu đề khiến bạn cực kỳ tức giận có thể được thiết kế để tác động đến bạn.

45.q: What does "The goal is to be aware, not overwhelmed" mean?
o: Read news all day so you never miss an important story.
Only watch good news.
Know nothing about the news.
Stay informed without letting the news destroy your peace of mind.
45.e: Câu kết của bài: được thông tin là quan trọng nhưng không để nó lấn át mình.

45.q: The writer's uncle used to be a newspaper editor.
45.e: Ông chú là biên tập viên báo đã nghỉ hưu.

45.q: According to the text, people who are arrested are always guilty.
45.e: Người bị bắt không nhất thiết có tội; họ vô tội cho đến khi được chứng minh ngược lại.

45.q: The writer now reads the news mainly in the evening.
45.e: Giờ tác giả đọc tin chủ yếu vào buổi sáng.

45.q: The writer reads two or three sources with different political views.
45.e: Tác giả đọc từ hai, ba nguồn đáng tin có quan điểm chính trị khác nhau.

45.q: How do you usually get your news? Write two rules from the text that you think are useful, and explain why.
45.h: Mô tả thói quen đọc tin hiện tại, rồi chọn 2 lời khuyên trong bài và giải thích bằng "This is useful because…".

46.q: Why did the writer join the science fair?
o: She wanted to win a prize.
She loved science more than any other subject.
Her friend Phong convinced her.
The teacher forced her.
46.e: Tác giả suýt không tham gia; người bạn mê kỹ thuật thuyết phục cô vào nhóm.

46.q: What was the team's experiment about?
o: Measuring the temperature of a pond
Building a small robot that could clean a pond
Growing plants without soil
Cleaning dirty water with cheap, natural materials
46.e: Câu hỏi nghiên cứu được nêu rõ.

46.q: What did the team do when the first results were disappointing?
o: They bought a new filter.
They asked the teacher to do it.
They gave up and chose a different, easier experiment.
They analysed the data again and changed the sand.
46.e: Thay vì bỏ cuộc, họ phân tích lại và thay cát mịn hơn.

46.q: According to the teacher, a scientific conclusion must be based on …
o: what you hope to find
the judges' ideas
the teacher's opinion
evidence
46.e: Kết luận khoa học phải dựa trên bằng chứng.

46.q: What did the writer realize at the end?
o: Robots are more interesting than water.
She had never been given the chance to experiment, fail and try again.
She would never be good at science, however hard she tried.
She should study engineering at university, like her friend Phong.
46.e: Tác giả nhận ra mình không "dở khoa học", chỉ là chưa có cơ hội.

46.q: The team collected water samples from a pond near the school.
46.e: Họ lấy mẫu nước từ một cái ao gần trường.

46.q: After changing the sand, the water came out completely brown.
46.e: Sau khi thay cát và thêm một lớp, nước chảy ra gần như trong.

46.q: The team won first prize at the fair.
46.e: Đội không giành giải nhất; một đội làm robot nhỏ đã thắng.

46.q: The judge from the laboratory offered the writer a job.
46.e: Giám khảo chỉ nhận xét dự án thực tế và hữu ích; bài không nói đến công việc.

46.q: Describe a time when you tried something, failed at first, and then improved. What did you change?
46.h: Kể bằng thì quá khứ đơn; dùng "At first… / Instead of giving up, I… / This time…" để mô tả quá trình.

47.q: What did the writer think of poetry at school?
o: It was old-fashioned and difficult.
It was easy to understand.
It was exciting and modern, but too long.
It was her favourite subject.
47.e: Thơ trong sách giáo khoa có vẻ cũ kỹ và khó.

47.q: What made the writer start loving poetry?
o: A short poem that described exactly what she felt during a difficult time
A teacher's lesson about a poem by a famous classical poet
A poetry competition
A film about a poet's life
47.e: Trong một năm khó khăn, cô đọc một bài thơ ngắn diễn tả đúng cảm xúc của mình.

47.q: According to the writer, how is a poem different from a novel?
o: A poem can capture a feeling in a single image.
A poem has a plot and chapters.
A poem is always longer and more difficult to read.
A poem is easier to write.
47.e: Khác với tiểu thuyết, thơ nắm bắt cảm xúc chỉ trong một hình ảnh.

47.q: Why does the writer write her own poems?
o: To help her reflect and turn painful moments into something meaningful
To win competitions
To publish a book of poems and become a well-known poet one day
To make money
47.e: Viết giúp cô suy ngẫm và biến khoảnh khắc đau buồn thành điều có ý nghĩa.

47.q: What does the writer suggest to people who think poetry is not for them?
o: Write a long poem.
Try a modern poet or listen to a poet reading their own work.
Read only classical poets because they are the best.
Take a poetry course at a university or a small studio.

47.q: The writer bought the book of translated poems in a small bookshop.
47.e: Cô mua cuốn thơ dịch ở một hiệu sách nhỏ.

47.q: The writer read the book until two in the morning.
47.e: Cô đọc đến hai giờ sáng.

47.q: The writer plans to publish her poems soon.
47.e: Cô nói có lẽ sẽ không bao giờ xuất bản.

47.q: The writer's poems have been performed in the studio.
47.e: Bài nói các nhà thơ trẻ trình diễn ở studio, không nói thơ của tác giả được trình diễn.

47.q: Is there a song, poem or book that once described exactly how you felt? Write about it and explain why it was meaningful to you.
47.h: Giới thiệu tác phẩm, hoàn cảnh bạn gặp nó (thì quá khứ), và lý do nó có ý nghĩa (It helped me… / It made me realize…).

48.q: What is the text mainly about?
o: Why horror stories are dangerous for young children
The writer's childhood summers at her aunt's cottage and what they taught her
How to become a farmer and keep bees in the countryside
How to keep bees safely
48.e: Bài kể những mùa hè ở nhà dì và bài học về điều thực sự quan trọng.

48.q: What two things was the aunt?
o: A cook and a photographer
A doctor and a musician
A farmer and an artist
A teacher and a writer
48.e: Dì vừa là nông dân vừa là nghệ sĩ.

48.q: Why did the writer stay silent and calm near the bees?
o: So she could hear them sing
Because she was afraid of the fox
So they would not bite her
Because her aunt was sleeping
48.e: Giữ im lặng và bình tĩnh để ong không đốt.

48.q: What did the aunt love telling at night?
o: Horror and mystery stories
History lessons
Funny jokes about her neighbours
Stories about her travels
48.e: Dì thích truyện kinh dị và bí ẩn, và rất giỏi làm bọn trẻ sợ.

48.q: What does the writer do today when city life feels too fast?
o: She visits the cottage every weekend with her cousins.
She keeps bees on her balcony.
She closes her eyes and returns there in spirit.
She plays with her cousins.
48.e: Tác giả nhắm mắt và trở về căn nhà nhỏ "trong tâm tưởng".

48.q: The cottage had a leaking roof.
48.e: Căn nhà gỗ nhỏ có mái dột.

48.q: The children collected shells and stones from the bank of the river.
48.e: Bọn trẻ nhặt lá, vỏ sò và đá nhẵn bên bờ sông.

48.q: The children's fears continued in the morning.
48.e: Đến sáng, khi mặt trời lên, mọi nỗi sợ biến mất.

48.q: The aunt sold her coloured cloth at the market.
48.e: Bài chỉ nói dì làm vải màu từ len và bông, không nói dì có bán hay không.

48.q: Describe a place from your childhood where you felt free and happy. What did you do there, and what did it teach you about what really matters?
48.h: Mô tả nơi chốn bằng thì quá khứ và tính từ cảm giác (peaceful, relaxing…); kết bằng "It taught me that…".

49.q: What challenged the writer to start running?
o: A colleague who said he could finish a marathon in a year
A television programme about famous runners
A bet with his brother
A doctor's advice after a health check at work
49.e: Một đồng nghiệp từng vô địch giải chạy địa phương đã thách anh.

49.q: What was the writer's goal for the marathon?
o: To run faster than his colleague
To cross the finish line
To raise money for charity
To win a medal
49.e: Mục tiêu đơn giản là về đến đích.

49.q: What did the writer learn about increasing distance?
o: Only run long distances.
Increase it as fast as possible to finish the race sooner.
If you increase it too fast, you will get injured.
Distance does not matter.
49.e: Tăng cự ly quá nhanh chắc chắn sẽ bị chấn thương.

49.q: What advice did a stranger give at kilometre thirty?
o: Don't look too far ahead; just reach the next tree.
Run faster to finish sooner.
Drink more water.
Stop and rest for ten minutes, then start again slowly.
49.e: Lời khuyên của người lạ chạy bên cạnh.

49.q: What does the writer mean by "big goals are reached in small pieces"?
o: Big goals need big teams.
You should choose small goals only, because they are easier.
Big goals are impossible for most people.
You reach big goals by achieving many small steps.
49.e: Giống như "chạy đến cái cây tiếp theo", mục tiêu lớn đạt được bằng nhiều bước nhỏ.

49.q: Two years ago, the writer could not run for more than ten minutes.
49.e: Hai năm trước, anh không chạy được quá mười phút.

49.q: The writer only trained when the weather was good.
49.e: Anh tập theo kế hoạch dù trời mưa, lạnh hay rất nóng.

49.q: The writer saw a man running backwards in the race.
49.e: Trong số người chạy có cả một người chạy giật lùi.

49.q: The writer's colleague also ran in the same marathon.
49.e: Bài không nói đồng nghiệp có tham gia cuộc đua hay không.

49.q: Think of a big goal you have. How could you break it into small pieces? Describe the first three steps.
49.h: Nêu mục tiêu lớn, rồi chia thành 3 bước bằng "First, I will… / Then… / After that…"; nêu cách bạn giữ động lực khi muốn bỏ cuộc.

50.q: What was the writer like as a traveller before?
o: Careless and always worried
Afraid of flying
Very organized and calm
Rich and relaxed
50.e: Tác giả mang quá nhiều đồ, luôn vội vàng và lo lắng suốt chuyến đi.

50.q: What did the writer do differently on the trip to the mountain village?
o: He booked early, exchanged money before leaving and carried one small bag.
He stayed in a luxury hotel.
He travelled with a big group.
He took a heavy suitcase so that he would have everything he might need.
50.e: Đặt phòng sớm, đổi tiền trước và chỉ mang một túi nhỏ.

50.q: How did the writer get invited to a wedding ceremony?
o: A photographer he met invited him.
The hotel organized it for its guests.
He knew the bride.
He saw an advertisement.
50.e: Một nhiếp ảnh gia đang làm album về văn hóa dân gian mời anh đến đám cưới.

50.q: What happened on the last day?
o: He missed his flight.
He lost his passport again.
There was a small earthquake.
There was a big festival in the square.
50.e: Ngày cuối có một trận động đất nhỏ.

50.q: What does "the less we carry, the more we notice" also apply to?
o: Our phones
Our money
Only suitcases
Our minds
50.e: Bài học áp dụng cho cả vali lẫn tâm trí.

50.q: The writer once left his passport in a shopping mall.
50.e: Có lần anh để quên hộ chiếu trong trung tâm mua sắm và suýt lỡ chuyến.

50.q: The writer exchanged money at the airport.
50.e: Anh đổi tiền trước khi đi để khỏi xếp hàng ở sân bay.

50.q: The village had many fashionable shops.
50.e: Làng không có cửa hàng thời trang nào.

50.q: Some old houses were damaged in the earthquake.
50.e: Không ai bị thương nhưng vài ngôi nhà cổ bị hư hại.

50.q: Do you usually pack too much or too little when you travel? Describe how you would plan a "light" trip.
50.h: Dùng thì hiện tại đơn cho thói quen, rồi "I would…" để lên kế hoạch: mang gì, đặt chỗ thế nào, làm gì ở nơi đến.

51.q: What did the writer imagine running a business would mainly be about?
o: Hiring people
Advertising
Baking
Managing money
51.e: Trước đây anh nghĩ điều hành kinh doanh chủ yếu là làm bánh.

51.q: What problem appeared in the first year?
o: The employees left.
The oven broke and he had to close the shop for a month.
A big commercial bakery opened on the same street.
The bank closed his account.
51.e: Một tiệm bánh thương mại lớn mở trên cùng con phố với giá rẻ hơn một chút.

51.q: What did the customers say they wanted?
o: More types of cake and sweet bread
The lowest price in the area
Fresh bread, friendly service and a place to sit
Home delivery
51.e: Khách không quan tâm giá thấp nhất mà muốn bánh tươi, phục vụ thân thiện và chỗ ngồi.

51.q: How did the bakery become different from the large bakery?
o: It became a place where people knew each other's names.
It sold only cakes.
It became cheaper than the large bakery on the street.
It opened 24 hours a day.
51.e: Khác với tiệm lớn, tiệm của anh thành nơi mọi người biết tên nhau.

51.q: According to the writer, what is failure?
o: Part of the process
Something to avoid at all costs
The opposite of success
A sign to stop
51.e: Thất bại không phải là đối lập của thành công mà là một phần của quá trình.

51.q: The writer had a lot of experience in management.
51.e: Anh không có kinh nghiệm quản lý.

51.q: There were months when the writer could not pay himself.
51.e: Có những tháng anh không trả lương được cho chính mình.

51.q: The bakery now employs five people.
51.e: Hiện tiệm có năm nhân viên và dự định mở cửa hàng thứ hai.

51.q: The large commercial bakery closed down.
51.e: Bài không nói tiệm lớn có đóng cửa hay không.

51.q: If you opened a small business, what would it be? How would you make it different from bigger competitors?
51.h: Dùng câu điều kiện loại 2 (If I opened…, I would…); nêu 2 điểm khác biệt và lý do khách hàng sẽ thích.

52.q: What did the writer's parents bring when they came to the country?
o: Many relatives who already lived there
A lot of money from selling their house
Their own small business
Almost nothing except a suitcase and a belief in education
52.e: Bố mẹ đến với gần như không có gì ngoài chiếc vali và niềm tin vào giáo dục.

52.q: How did the writer feel as a child?
o: She felt more at home at school.
She did not notice any difference.
She felt she did not completely belong anywhere.
She felt proud of her two cultures from an early age.
52.e: Hồi nhỏ, tác giả cảm thấy mình không hoàn toàn thuộc về nơi nào.

52.q: What made the writer feel proud for the first time?
o: Visiting her parents' country for the first time
Learning a new language
Interviewing her grandmother for a history project
Winning a rugby match for her school
52.e: Phỏng vấn bà cho bài tập lịch sử giúp tác giả thấy gia đình mình dũng cảm thế nào.

52.q: How does the writer use her background at work?
o: She organizes religious festivals for her community.
She helps with translation and explains cultural differences.
She teaches history at a secondary school.
She works for an airline.
52.e: Ở chỗ làm, cô hỗ trợ dịch và giải thích khác biệt văn hóa cho đồng nghiệp.

52.q: Why does the writer dislike the question "Where are you really from?"
o: It is too personal to ask a stranger.
She does not know the answer.
It is asked too often by her family.
It suggests she is not equal to others.
52.e: Câu hỏi ngụ ý rằng cô không bình đẳng với người khác.

52.q: The writer played rugby at school.
52.e: Ở trường, cô nói tiếng Anh và chơi bóng bầu dục.

52.q: The writer's relatives said her accent had become "too foreign".
52.e: Họ hàng nói giọng của cô đã trở nên "quá ngoại quốc".

52.q: The writer feels she must choose one culture.
52.e: Cô không còn thấy mình phải chọn.

52.q: The writer's grandmother still lives in her village.
52.e: Bà kể về ngôi làng và hành trình đến cuộc sống mới; bài không nói hiện nay bà sống ở đâu.

52.q: What different "worlds" or groups are part of your identity (for example family, school, hometown, online)? How do you connect them?
52.h: Liệt kê 2–3 nhóm, mô tả bạn khác nhau thế nào ở mỗi nơi, và nêu điều giúp bạn là "một con người trọn vẹn".

53.q: What did the writer believe when she first arrived on campus?
o: Grades were not important.
The smartest students studied the longest.
Clever students never needed to study very hard.
Group study was the best method.
53.e: Ban đầu tác giả nghĩ người thông minh nhất là người học lâu nhất.

53.q: Why is reading the same text again and again "not worth much"?
o: It takes too little time.
It is too difficult for most students to concentrate.
It only makes the material feel familiar.
It damages your eyes.
53.e: Đọc đi đọc lại chỉ khiến tài liệu "có vẻ quen".

53.q: What is a better technique than rereading, according to the text?
o: Reading faster
Closing the book and summarizing the main points from memory
Highlighting every line in a different colour so you can find it later
Copying long quotes into your notes
53.e: Gấp sách lại và tóm tắt các ý chính bằng trí nhớ.

53.q: How did the writer change her exam revision?
o: She only revised with friends.
She revised everything the night before.
She stopped revising.
She spread revision over several weeks.
53.e: Thay vì ôn dồn đêm trước, cô trải ra nhiều tuần.

53.q: What does the writer mean by "you may be working very hard in the wrong direction"?
o: You should stop studying and find a job instead.
Without the right strategy, hard work may not bring good results.
Directions are hard to follow.
You should change your university.
53.e: Chăm chỉ quan trọng, nhưng chiến lược cũng quan trọng không kém.

53.q: A senior student gave the writer advice that changed her approach.
53.e: Một sinh viên năm cuối sắp tốt nghiệp đã khuyên cô.

53.q: According to the text, the brain builds connections between related ideas.
53.e: Kết hợp các môn học giúp não tự nhiên tạo liên kết giữa các ý liên quan.

53.q: The writer's results improved only after two years.
53.e: Chỉ trong một học kỳ, kết quả đã cải thiện rõ rệt.

53.q: The study adviser was a professor of psychology.
53.e: Bài chỉ nói tác giả hẹn gặp một cố vấn học tập; không nói người đó là ai.

53.q: Which study technique from the text would help you the most? Explain how you would use it for a subject you are studying now.
53.h: Chọn một kỹ thuật (tự tóm tắt, tự kiểm tra, ôn giãn cách…), giải thích vì sao, và mô tả cách áp dụng cho một môn cụ thể.

54.q: What happened in the writer's family when people disagreed?
o: They wrote letters to each other.
They asked a friend to help.
They argued loudly at the dinner table.
They stopped talking, sometimes for days.
54.e: Khi bất đồng, mọi người im lặng, có khi kéo dài nhiều ngày.

54.q: What was the problem with the colleague?
o: He was often late for meetings with clients.
He was rude to customers.
He never shared his work.
He took credit for the writer's ideas in meetings.
54.e: Người đồng nghiệp nhiều lần nhận công ý tưởng của tác giả trong các cuộc họp.

54.q: According to the course teacher, what is the goal of a conflict?
o: To avoid the other person in future
To reach a better understanding
To show you are right
To win the argument
54.e: Mục tiêu không phải thắng tranh luận mà là hiểu nhau hơn.

54.q: Which sentence follows the rule "talk about the behaviour, not the person"?
o: "You are dishonest."
"You mentioned my idea without referring to me, and I felt uncomfortable."
"You never think about others."
"You are a careless guy who never listens to anyone in this team."
54.e: Câu mẫu trong bài mô tả hành vi cụ thể và cảm xúc của mình, không chỉ trích con người.

54.q: What happened when the writer talked to his colleague?
o: The colleague got angry and refused to talk about it.
The colleague left the company soon after the conversation.
Their manager joined the conversation.
The colleague apologized and explained he had been under pressure.
54.e: Người đồng nghiệp xin lỗi và giải thích mình đang chịu áp lực.

54.q: The colleague's behaviour bothered the writer so much that he could not sleep.
54.e: Tác giả tự nhủ không sao, nhưng thực ra bực đến mất ngủ.

54.q: The communication teacher was a man.
54.e: Người dạy là một phụ nữ (The lady who taught it).

54.q: According to the text, most arguments are more about feelings than facts.
54.e: Hầu hết các cuộc tranh cãi liên quan đến cảm xúc nhiều hơn sự thật.

54.q: The writer's colleague was later promoted.
54.e: Bài không nói gì về việc thăng chức.

54.q: Think of a disagreement you had with someone. Rewrite what you said (or could say) using the three rules from the text.
54.h: Kể ngắn gọn tình huống, rồi viết lại lời nói theo ba quy tắc: nói về hành vi, lắng nghe, tìm điểm đồng thuận (I felt… when… / I understand that…).

55.q: When did the writer become a fan of detective fiction?
o: At university
At twelve
At five
After his uncle died
55.e: Từ năm mười hai tuổi, khi chú tặng một cuốn tiểu thuyết trinh thám cũ.

55.q: How does a good detective reach a conclusion?
o: By asking the police what they think happened
By guessing quickly
By collecting clues and rejecting explanations that do not fit the facts
By trusting her first impression of every person in the house
55.e: Thám tử giỏi không vội kết luận mà thu thập manh mối và loại bỏ giả thuyết không khớp.

55.q: How did the writer apply the detective method when a friend seemed annoyed?
o: He looked for clues and asked questions before deciding.
He asked another friend.
He stopped talking to her until she explained.
He assumed the worst.
55.e: Anh cố không nghĩ điều tệ nhất mà tìm manh mối và hỏi trước.

55.q: According to the writer, how is real life different from many detective novels?
o: Detectives in real life are smarter and always find the person who committed the crime.
There are no crimes in real life.
In real life, the guilty are not always punished and innocent people sometimes are.
Real life is simpler.
55.e: Đời thực phức tạp hơn: có người vô tội bị phạt, có kẻ có tội thoát.

55.q: What skill does the writer say detective stories can improve?
o: Memory for names and faces
Cooking
Critical thinking
Public speaking
55.e: Tác giả giới thiệu thể loại này cho ai muốn cải thiện tư duy phản biện.

55.q: In the first novel, a rich gentleman was poisoned at dinner.
55.e: Một quý ông giàu có bị đầu độc trong bữa tối.

55.q: In that novel, only the servant had a reason to commit the crime.
55.e: Mọi khách, người hầu và cả chủ nhà đều có động cơ.

55.q: At first, the writer read detective stories simply for entertainment.
55.e: Lúc đầu anh chỉ đọc để giải trí.

55.q: The writer has written his own detective novel.
55.e: Bài không nói anh có viết tiểu thuyết.

55.q: Describe a time when you jumped to a conclusion about someone or something and later found out you were wrong. What clues did you miss?
55.h: Kể bằng thì quá khứ đơn và quá khứ hoàn thành (I thought…, but later I found out that… had…); nêu bài học rút ra.

o: Part of a radio interview with an architect
A letter from an architect to his son
A school report about buildings in the city
A magazine article written by Mr Hai himself
56.e: Đây là một phần cuộc phỏng vấn trên đài phát thanh.

56.q: Why was Mr Hai's birth recorded at the local temple?
o: His father was a priest at the local temple.
It was a family tradition for every child.
The temple was next to his house.
There was no proper government office then.

56.q: How did Mr Hai begin his career?
o: A company director saw his drawings and let him work in the office.
He studied architecture at a famous university in the capital.
His father was an architect.
He won a design competition for young people.
56.e: Giám đốc một công ty xây dựng thấy bản vẽ và cho ông làm trong văn phòng.

56.q: According to Mr Hai, who should a building serve?
o: Rich and powerful people
Magazines and advertising companies
The architect himself
The individual people who use it
56.e: Bí quyết của ông là tòa nhà phải phục vụ con người cụ thể sử dụng nó.

56.q: What does Mr Hai say about mistakes?
o: They are the best teachers if you recognize them.
They should be hidden.
He never made any serious mistakes in his career.
They are always expensive.
56.e: Sai lầm là người thầy tốt nhất nếu ta nhận ra chúng.

56.q: Mr Hai's mother was a chef in a pub near the station.
56.e: Mẹ ông là đầu bếp ở quán rượu nhỏ gần ga.

56.q: Mr Hai was very good at mathematics.
56.e: Toán học là "cơn ác mộng" đối với ông.

56.q: Some of Mr Hai's early projects were too expensive.
56.e: Ông thừa nhận một số dự án ban đầu quá tốn kém.

56.q: Mr Hai still works as an architect every day.
56.e: Ông khuyên tiếp tục học hỏi "kể cả ở tuổi 90", nhưng không nói ông còn làm việc hằng ngày.

56.q: Imagine you are interviewing someone you admire. Write three questions and the answers you think they would give.
56.h: Viết theo dạng hội thoại (Me: … / Name: …); dùng các câu hỏi Wh- (How did you…? What is your secret…?).

57.q: What is the main lesson of the text?
o: Old things are always valuable, so families should keep them forever.
You should never throw anything away.
Charity shops need more donations.
A person's life is in the people and memories, not in possessions.
57.e: Cuộc đời của ông không nằm trong đồ đạc mà ở những người ông yêu và ký ức ông để lại.

57.q: Why had the grandfather moved a double bed downstairs?
o: He wanted to sleep near the TV.
The bedroom was too cold.
The upstairs was being repaired.
He could no longer use the lift.
57.e: Ông chuyển giường xuống tầng dưới khi không dùng được thang máy nữa.

57.q: Why did the grandfather meet the president?
o: He was a politician and worked with the president for many years.
He won a national prize for his electronic inventions.
He played music at a ceremony.
He designed the president's house.
57.e: Bức ảnh ông bắt tay tổng thống khi giành giải thưởng quốc gia.

57.q: Why could the family not keep everything?
o: Their flat was too small and many items were broken or dusty.
The neighbours wanted the house.
They needed money and sold most of it online.
The grandfather asked them in a letter to give everything away.
57.e: Căn hộ quá nhỏ và nhiều món đã hỏng hoặc phủ bụi.

o: A young man who repaired old radios
A charity shop
A teacher for her school library
The writer's mother
57.e: Một cô giáo lấy sách cho thư viện trường.

57.q: The grandfather had not played his musical instrument for thirty years.
57.e: Nhạc cụ đã ba mươi năm ông không chơi.

57.q: The grandfather bought a postcard of the queen in Paris.
57.e: Ông mua tấm bưu thiếp ở London.

57.q: The family kept the ring the grandfather gave the grandmother.
57.e: Họ giữ lại chiếc nhẫn, những lá thư, hộp thuốc lá và ảnh.

57.q: The family sold the grandfather's house to a neighbour.
57.e: Bài nói hàng xóm lấy đồ, không nói gì về việc bán nhà.

57.q: Choose one object you own that has real emotional value. Describe it and explain the story behind it.
57.h: Mô tả đồ vật (It is a…, It was given to me by…), kể câu chuyện bằng thì quá khứ và giải thích vì sao bạn quý nó.

58.q: What was the writer's bad habit?
o: Arriving late
Comparing herself with everyone
Checking the news all day
Spending too much money online
58.e: Thói quen xấu được nêu ngay ở câu đầu.

o: She read a book about happiness.
She lost her job.
A friend gave her advice about social media.
A thief stole her phone at a train station.
58.e: Không có điện thoại, cô chỉ còn biết nhìn xung quanh và suy nghĩ.

58.q: What does "comparing my first chapter with someone else's twentieth" mean?
o: Other people write better than her.
Some books are much longer than others, so they are harder to finish.
She should read more books.
It is unfair to compare your beginning with someone else's later success.
58.e: Phép so sánh ẩn dụ: so khởi đầu của mình với giai đoạn thành công của người khác là không công bằng.

58.q: What does the writer track now?
o: Her monthly spending
Her social media followers
Other people's progress online
Her own progress and small wins
58.e: Cô theo dõi tiến bộ của bản thân thay vì của người khác.

58.q: Why does the writer celebrate other people's success sincerely?
o: Her friends asked her to.
She wants them to celebrate her success in the same way.
It is polite.
Their wins do not take anything away from hers.
58.e: Thành công của người khác không lấy đi gì của mình.

58.q: At first, the writer was furious when her phone was stolen.
58.e: Ban đầu cô rất tức giận.

58.q: The writer deleted all her social media apps.
58.e: Cô xóa hai ứng dụng và giữ lại một, dùng có giới hạn thời gian.

58.q: The old feelings sometimes return when the writer is tired.
58.e: Cảm giác cũ đôi khi quay lại, nhất là khi mệt.

58.q: The police found the writer's phone the next day.
58.e: Bài không nói điện thoại có được tìm thấy không.

58.q: Do you sometimes compare yourself with others? Write about one "small win" you had recently and why it matters to you.
58.h: Trả lời thật lòng câu hỏi đầu (I sometimes… when…), rồi kể một thành công nhỏ gần đây bằng thì quá khứ hoặc hiện tại hoàn thành.

59.q: Where was the company weekend held last year?
o: At a beach hotel by the sea
In the city centre
On a boat
At a ski resort in the mountains
59.e: Năm ngoái tổ chức ở khu trượt tuyết trên núi.

59.q: What did the writer discover about herself?
o: She was good at climbing and enjoyed the physical challenges.
She was the best at puzzles.
She was good at organizing people and keeping everyone calm.
She did not like teamwork.
59.e: Tác giả phát hiện mình giỏi tổ chức và giữ mọi người bình tĩnh.

59.q: How did the team approach each challenge?
o: The leader decided everything.
They worked separately.
They discussed the problem, divided the tasks and then acted.
They acted immediately and solved problems as quickly as possible.
59.e: Nhóm thảo luận trước, chia việc rồi mới hành động.

59.q: What did one colleague learn about herself?
o: She was better than the engineer.
She hated climbing and refused to try it.
She was not as shy as she thought.
She wanted a new job.
59.e: Cô luôn nghĩ mình nhút nhát nhưng lại dẫn dắt nhóm leo núi.

59.q: Which change did the writer make after returning home?
o: She changed teams.
She started working on weekends to finish her projects on time.
She started asking colleagues for their opinions more often.
She joined a ski club.
59.e: Một trong ba thay đổi là hỏi ý kiến đồng nghiệp thường xuyên hơn.

59.q: The writer almost did not go on the weekend.
59.e: Cô suýt kiếm cớ để không đi.

59.q: The writer's team won all five challenges.
59.e: Nhóm về nhất ba trên năm thử thách.

59.q: The quiet reader noticed details that others missed.
59.e: Người hay đọc triết học, ít nói, nhận ra những chi tiết người khác bỏ sót.

59.q: The sales manager was the team leader in the rock climb.
59.e: Người dẫn dắt nhóm leo núi là đồng nghiệp tự cho mình nhút nhát; trưởng phòng bán hàng giữ tinh thần tích cực cho cả nhóm.

59.q: Describe a group or team you were part of. What role did you play, and what hidden talent did you or someone else discover?
59.h: Kể bằng thì quá khứ; mô tả vai trò của từng người (X was good at… / I was responsible for…) và điều bất ngờ bạn phát hiện.

60.q: What is the writer's attitude to smartphones?
o: He has stopped using a phone.
He admires the technology but uses his phone more consciously now.
He thinks they only make people happy.
He thinks smartphones should be banned for people under thirty years old.
60.e: Tác giả ngưỡng mộ kỹ thuật nhưng giờ dùng điện thoại có ý thức hơn.

60.q: What did the writer's analysis of his phone use show?
o: He never read advertisements.
He used it less than his friends.
He used it only for work and to pay bills.
He picked up his phone ninety times a day.
60.e: Anh cầm điện thoại lên chín mươi lần mỗi ngày.

60.q: According to researchers, how does heavy social media use affect mood?
o: It encourages comparison and reduces time for sleep, reading and friends.
It has no effect, because most people use it only for a short time each day.
It improves concentration.
It always makes people happier.
60.e: Tác động gián tiếp: khuyến khích so sánh và lấy đi thời gian ngủ, đọc sách, gặp bạn.

60.q: What environmental cost of smartphones does the text mention?
o: They cause forest fires.
They are difficult to recycle at home.
They create a lot of noise pollution in cities, especially at night.
Producing and importing them uses huge amounts of energy and rare metals.
60.e: Sản xuất và nhập khẩu thiết bị cần năng lượng khổng lồ và kim loại hiếm.

60.q: What does "it should work for us, not the other way round" mean?
o: We should work harder with phones.
Phones are better than people.
We should control the phone, not let the phone control us.
Phones should do our jobs so that we have more free time.
60.e: Điện thoại nên phục vụ ta chứ không phải ta phục vụ nó.
Tác giả làm trong ngành công nghệ thông tin.

60.q: The writer still keeps his phone in the bedroom at night.
60.e: Anh cấm điện thoại vào phòng ngủ và sạc nó trong bếp.

60.q: The writer uses a cheap alarm clock now.
60.e: Anh dùng một chiếc đồng hồ báo thức rẻ tiền.

60.q: The writer's family also changed their phone habits.
60.e: Bài không nhắc đến gia đình tác giả.

60.q: Do you think your phone makes you happier or less happy? Give two examples from your own life and one rule you could follow.
60.h: Nêu quan điểm, đưa hai ví dụ cụ thể (một tích cực, một tiêu cực), rồi đặt một quy tắc bằng "From now on, I will…".

61.q: What did the writer expect before visiting the museum?
o: A film about the war
An exciting adventure
A sad lecture from a guide
A boring row of glass cases
61.e: Tác giả nghĩ sẽ thấy một dãy tủ kính nhàm chán.

61.q: What did the soldier write in the last entry of his diary?
o: He had won the battle.
He wanted to go home and see his mother and his little sister again.
"Tomorrow we go forward. I wonder if I will see the sea again."
He hated the enemy.
61.e: Dòng nhật ký cuối viết đêm trước khi anh hy sinh.

61.q: What did the letters from enemy soldiers show?
o: They were cruel and cold, and they did not care about the people they fought.
They were older and stronger.
They wanted to win at any cost.
They were young, frightened and homesick, like the writer's own soldiers.
61.e: Lính phía bên kia cũng trẻ, sợ hãi và nhớ nhà.

61.q: Why did the teacher say they visited the museum?
o: To learn to hate the enemy
To prepare for a history exam the next week
To see famous weapons
So that they never repeat these mistakes

61.q: According to the writer, the most important lesson of history is about …
o: dates and battles
empathy
politics
weapons
61.e: Bài học quan trọng nhất là sự đồng cảm.

61.q: The museum also showed the side of the enemy.
61.e: Bảo tàng cũng thể hiện phía bên kia qua thư của lính đối phương.

61.q: The bomb in the first room had exploded.
61.e: Đó là quả bom chưa phát nổ.

61.q: Everyone on the bus talked about the visit on the way home.
61.e: Trên xe về không ai nói gì.

61.q: The writer's grandfather fought in the war.
61.e: Bài không nhắc đến ông của tác giả.

61.q: Why do you think it is important to learn about past wars? Write your opinion with one example from a museum, a film or a book.
61.h: Nêu quan điểm (I believe it is important to… because…), một ví dụ cụ thể và điều bạn học được về sự đồng cảm.

62.q: Why did the writer need a car?
o: His father gave him money.
He wanted to start a taxi business.
He got a job in a town with poor public transport.
His old car broke down on the way to work.
62.e: Anh có việc ở một thị trấn giao thông công cộng kém.

o: Only buy a new car.
Never buy a car the first time you see it; investigate and compare.
Buy the cheapest car you can find, because all used cars have problems.
Buy from a friend.

62.q: Why did the writer walk away from the second seller?
o: The seller was rude.
The car was too small.
The price was too high and the seller refused to discuss it.
The seller refused to let him drive the car on the main road.
62.e: Người bán không cho lái thử ra đường chính; theo bố anh, giấu giếm thường nghĩa là có vấn đề.

62.q: Why did the writer choose the elderly couple's car?
o: It was the most fashionable car he could afford in the town.
It was the cheapest.
It had been treated with care and had all its service documents.
It was a racing car.
62.e: Chiếc xe được giữ gìn cẩn thận và có đầy đủ giấy tờ bảo dưỡng.

62.q: What lesson did the writer learn beyond cars?
o: Ask your father before every decision.
Do your research, trust facts and be prepared to say no.
Never make big decisions.
Always trust the promises of people who seem honest.
62.e: Bài học được tóm lại ở câu cuối.

62.q: The writer could not afford a new car.
62.e: Anh không đủ tiền mua xe mới nên quyết định mua xe cũ.

62.q: The car the writer bought is very beautiful.
62.e: Chiếc xe nhỏ và hơi xấu.

62.q: The writer paid a little extra for new tyres.
62.e: Hai bên thỏa thuận giá hợp lý, cộng thêm một ít tiền cho lốp mới.

62.q: The writer has had problems with his car since he bought it.
62.e: Chiếc xe vẫn đáng tin cậy suốt ba năm.

62.q: Describe a big purchase or decision you made (or will make). How did you research it, and what would you do differently?
62.h: Kể quá trình bằng thì quá khứ (First, I checked… / Then I compared…), hoặc lên kế hoạch bằng "will"; kết bằng một bài học.

63.q: Why was the writer frightened when his brother asked him to give a speech?
o: He was ill.
He did not know the bride.
He did not like his brother's new wife and her family.
He is not a confident speaker and was afraid of embarrassing him.
63.e: Tác giả không tự tin khi nói và sợ làm anh trai xấu hổ.

63.q: What advice did the bride give the writer?
o: Make people laugh with a lot of jokes.
Be honest and talk about who he is.
Read from a book.
Keep the speech very short.
63.e: Lời khuyên của chị dâu tương lai.

63.q: What story did the writer tell in his speech?
o: How his brother met the bride at university
How his brother got his first job
How his brother taught him to ride a bike
How they travelled together
63.e: Câu chuyện người anh dạy em đi xe đạp, chạy theo hàng giờ không phàn nàn.

63.q: What was special about the bride's dress?
o: It was very expensive and made in Paris.
It was designed by the writer.
It was red.
It had once belonged to her mother.
63.e: Chiếc váy trắng từng thuộc về mẹ cô dâu.

63.q: What did the writer realize about marriage?
o: It is only for young people.
It is about the ring.
It is a decision to face life's difficulties together every day.
It is mainly a big celebration for the two families and their friends.

63.q: The writer's father rang all the relatives when he saw the ring.
63.e: Bố tác giả gọi ngay cho tất cả họ hàng.

63.q: The ceremony took place outdoors by the river.
63.e: Buổi lễ diễn ra trong nhà, ở một hội trường cổ gần sông.

63.q: An aunt said the speech was the best part of the evening.
63.e: Một bà dì nói đó là phần hay nhất buổi tối.

63.q: The couple's two families had the same background.
63.e: Hai gia đình có xuất thân khác nhau và cuối cùng đã gắn kết.

63.q: Imagine you have to give a short speech at a friend's or family member's wedding. Write the speech, including one personal story.
63.h: Mở đầu bằng lời chào và giới thiệu mối quan hệ, kể một câu chuyện ngắn bằng thì quá khứ, kết bằng lời chúc (I wish you… / May you…).

o: Advice the writer would give to his younger self
A story about a holiday he took at eighteen
An interview with a teacher
A report about teenagers
64.e: Tác giả liệt kê những bài học muốn chia sẻ với bản thân năm 18 tuổi.

64.q: What does the writer say about fear?
o: Fear helps you choose friends.
Fear is always right, so you should listen to it.
You should never feel fear.
Fear is normal but not a reliable adviser.
64.e: Sợ hãi là bình thường nhưng không phải người cố vấn đáng tin.

64.q: What kind of friends should you choose, according to the writer?
o: Friends who agree with everything
Friends who make you better and tell you the truth
Friends with a lot of money
Friends who make you feel comfortable and never criticize you
64.e: Chọn bạn khiến mình tốt hơn, không chỉ dễ chịu hơn.

64.q: What do many older workers regret, according to the text?
o: Not travelling more
Not studying harder at school
Choosing money over meaning
Getting married too early
64.e: Nhiều người lao động lớn tuổi hối tiếc vì chọn tiền thay vì ý nghĩa.

64.q: According to the writer, what is success?
o: Being liked by everyone
A single big moment of luck
Earning a high salary
A mixture of small, repeated efforts
64.e: Thành công không phải một lần bùng nổ năng lượng mà là nhiều nỗ lực nhỏ lặp lại.

64.q: The writer says most of the things that frighten you will never happen.
64.e: Phần lớn những điều khiến ta sợ sẽ không bao giờ xảy ra.

64.q: The writer advises reading every clause before signing anything.
64.e: Đọc từng điều khoản trước khi ký.

64.q: The writer believes everyone will like you if you are kind.
64.e: Đừng mong ai cũng thích mình.

64.q: The writer is now a teacher.
64.e: Bài không nói tác giả làm nghề gì.

64.q: Write three pieces of advice to your younger self (for example at fifteen). Explain why each one matters.
64.h: Dùng câu mệnh lệnh (Do… / Don't…) cho mỗi lời khuyên, kèm một câu giải thích (because… / Otherwise…).

65.q: What job did the writer have at the camp?
o: Swimming teacher at the lake
Camp manager
Assistant to the leading instructor
Cook
65.e: Tác giả được thuê làm trợ lý cho người hướng dẫn chính, một giáo viên đã nghỉ hưu.

65.q: What did the writer learn about children and sweets?
o: Children do not like sweets at camp.
Children always share their sweets with other children.
Children rarely tell the truth when sweets are involved.
Parents always know about them.
65.e: Trẻ con hiếm khi nói thật khi có liên quan đến kẹo.

65.q: What did they do on rainy days?
o: They had boat races on the lake and swam with the instructor.
They flew kites on the hill.
They did photography projects, folded paper birds or invented games.
They went fishing.
65.e: Ngày mưa thì ở trong nhà làm các hoạt động khác.

65.q: What was the instructor's most important advice?
o: Never let children play outside.
Be strict with children so they follow the rules.
Watch their faces, not just their words.
Always give them sweets.
65.e: Lời khuyên của người hướng dẫn.

65.q: According to the writer, what is looking after others about?
o: Attention, patience and respect
Rules and punishment
Control and clear rules
Games and fun
65.e: Chăm sóc người khác không phải là kiểm soát.

65.q: The writer thought the job would be easy.
65.e: Anh tưởng đây là việc dễ, nhưng đã nhầm.

65.q: On the first day, the writer helped forty children.
65.e: Ngày đầu, anh giúp bốn mươi đứa trẻ vào trại.

65.q: The shy girl told the instructor about her neck immediately.
65.e: Cô bé quá sợ để nói với ai; người hướng dẫn tự nhận ra qua nét mặt.

65.q: The writer went back to work at the camp the next summer.
65.e: Bài không nói về mùa hè năm sau.

65.q: Have you ever looked after children or younger people? What did you learn? If not, what do you think would be the most difficult part?
65.h: Kể trải nghiệm bằng thì quá khứ, hoặc dùng "I think the most difficult part would be…" kèm lý do và cách xử lý.

66.q: What is the writer's main purpose in the text?
o: To share her experience of anxiety and encourage others to seek help
To describe her friend's depression
To criticize psychologists
To explain the science behind anxiety and how the brain reacts to fear
66.e: Bài kể trải nghiệm cá nhân và kết thúc bằng lời kêu gọi tìm kiếm sự giúp đỡ.

66.q: Why did the writer hesitate to ask for help?
o: She could not afford therapy because her income was too low at that time.
She did not want to seem dramatic and did not believe anything would work.
Her family did not allow it.
She did not know any psychologists.
66.e: Hai lý do được nêu bằng "partly because … partly because …".

66.q: What insight changed the writer's perspective?
o: Anxiety only affects weak people.
Anxiety is a normal reaction that has become too intense.
Anxiety can be cured in one session.
Anxiety is a personal weakness that you can control by relaxing more.
66.e: Nhận thức then chốt từ trị liệu.

66.q: What did the writer do when she wanted to avoid a difficult situation?
o: She stayed at home until the feeling of panic went away.
She faced it deliberately in small, manageable steps.
She took medication.
She called her friend.
66.e: Cô cố ý đối mặt với tình huống theo từng bước nhỏ.

66.q: The phrase "Recovery has not been a straight line" suggests that …
o: the writer's anxiety has disappeared completely.
recovery has had ups and downs.
recovery was very fast.
the writer has stopped therapy.
66.e: Hồi phục không theo đường thẳng, nghĩa là có lúc tốt lúc xấu; câu sau nói vẫn có giai đoạn lo âu.

66.q: From the outside, the writer's life looked stable.
66.e: Nhìn từ ngoài, cuộc sống của cô có vẻ ổn định.

66.q: In the first session, the therapist told the writer exactly what to do.
66.e: Nhà trị liệu không chỉ bảo phải làm gì mà chỉ đặt câu hỏi và lắng nghe.

66.q: The writer no longer has any anxiety attacks.
66.e: Các cơn vẫn xảy ra nhưng nhẹ hơn và cô hồi phục nhanh hơn.

66.q: The writer's friend is now a psychologist.
66.e: Bài chỉ nói người bạn từng bị trầm cảm và khuyên tác giả đi gặp chuyên gia.

66.q: The writer says that asking for help "takes real courage". Do you agree? Why do many people find it hard to ask for help, and how can we make it easier?
66.h: Nêu quan điểm, đưa 2 lý do khiến người ta ngại xin giúp đỡ, và 1–2 giải pháp (We could… / Schools and workplaces should…).

67.q: How did the writer's debt build up?
o: Through one big mistake: buying an expensive car he could not afford
Gradually, through loans, a credit card, a car and impulse buying
Because he lost his job
Because of medical bills
67.e: Nợ tích tụ dần dần từ nhiều nguồn.

67.q: What made the writer realize how serious his situation was?
o: The bank rejected his mortgage application.
His car was taken away.
His friends told him that he was spending too much on going out.
He received a letter from the police.
67.e: Ngân hàng từ chối hồ sơ vay mua nhà.

67.q: Which repayment strategy did the writer use?
o: Borrowing more to pay the old loans
Paying a small amount on every loan equally so that all of them go down
Focusing on the loan with the highest fee and interest first
Paying only the smallest loan
67.e: Ưu tiên khoản vay có phí và lãi suất cao nhất trước.

67.q: How much did the budget changes save, according to the writer's estimate?
o: About a tenth of his income
About half of his monthly income
Nothing at first
Roughly a fifth of his monthly income
67.e: Ước tính tiết kiệm khoảng một phần năm thu nhập hằng tháng.

67.q: How has the writer's relationship with money changed?
o: He now sees money mainly as a way to impress others and feel successful.
He spends more to reward himself.
He sees it as a tool for building a secure, independent future.
He no longer cares about money.
67.e: Tiền giờ là công cụ, không phải cách gây ấn tượng hay trốn tránh cảm xúc xấu.

67.q: At twenty-seven, the writer owed more than his yearly income.
67.e: Năm 27 tuổi, anh nợ nhiều hơn thu nhập một năm.

67.q: The writer kept his car to get to his part-time job.
The writer's friends sometimes teased him for not going out.
67.e: Bạn bè đôi khi trêu chọc vì anh từ chối đi chơi.

67.q: The writer has now bought a house with a mortgage.
67.e: Bài nói anh đã hết nợ, có quỹ khẩn cấp và tiết kiệm, nhưng không nói đã mua nhà.

67.q: What advice would you give a young person who has just received their first credit card? Use ideas from the text.
67.h: Đưa 3–4 lời khuyên (Make sure… / Avoid… / If you…, you should…) và giải thích hậu quả nếu không làm theo.

68.q: What did the writer assume leadership would mean?
o: Working alone
Doing the same work at a higher level
Having more holidays and a bigger office
Attending fewer meetings
68.e: Ban đầu anh nghĩ lãnh đạo chỉ là làm cùng công việc ở cấp cao hơn.

68.q: What feedback did a senior colleague give?
o: Your job is to enable other people to do their best work.
Work longer hours so that your team can see your example.
Avoid committee meetings.
Ask for a higher salary.
68.e: Nhận xét của đồng nghiệp cấp cao.

68.q: What did the writer discover many team members needed?
o: Recognition and a sense of purpose
More pressure and closer control
Longer deadlines
Higher salaries
68.e: Nhiều người không cần thêm áp lực mà cần được ghi nhận và có mục đích.

68.q: What does "manage upwards" mean in the text?
o: Get promoted quickly to a higher position in the company
Increase the team's targets
Manage people in a higher position, such as the chairman
Move to a higher floor
68.e: "Quản lý ngược lên": làm việc hiệu quả với cấp trên, ví dụ đề xuất phương án thay thế cho chủ tịch.

68.q: What is the writer's biggest lesson about leadership?
o: It is about meeting every deadline, even if the team has to work at weekends.
It is about status and control.
It is about creating an environment where people feel safe, respected and motivated.
It is about doing everything yourself.
68.e: Bài học lớn nhất ở đoạn cuối.

68.q: The writer missed several deadlines in his first month.
68.e: Anh trễ nhiều hạn chót và nhóm trở nên bực bội.

68.q: The writer ignored the conflict between two team members.
68.e: Anh mời hai người họp, nghe từng người và giúp họ thỏa hiệp.

68.q: The chairman rejected the writer's alternative plan.
68.e: Thật bất ngờ, ông đã chấp thuận.

68.q: The writer was promoted at the age of twenty-eight.
68.e: Anh được thăng chức trưởng nhóm năm 28 tuổi.

68.q: What makes a good leader, in your opinion? Describe a leader (a teacher, boss or team captain) you admire and what they did well.
68.h: Nêu 2–3 phẩm chất của người lãnh đạo giỏi, rồi minh họa bằng một người cụ thể (He/She always… / What I admire most is…).

o: A fall at home
An accident at the gym
A car accident on the way home
A sports match
69.e: Tác giả bị chấn thương cột sống do tai nạn ở phòng gym.

69.q: Why did the surgeon's explanation help the writer?
o: Her calm, honest explanation reduced his anxiety.
She used simple jokes.
It was very short and did not take much of his time.
She promised there were no risks.
69.e: Lời giải thích bình tĩnh, trung thực giúp giảm lo âu đáng kể.

69.q: Why did the writer find the first weeks humiliating?
o: His friends did not visit.
He could not work.
The hospital staff were rude to him and ignored his questions.
He was used to being active and now depended on others.
69.e: Một người quen chạy bộ mỗi sáng mà phải phụ thuộc người khác thì thấy nhục nhã.

o: Stop drinking water.
Eat less food and lose weight.
Eat more protein and vitamins.
Only eat vegetables.
69.e: Chuyên gia dinh dưỡng khuyên ăn nhiều protein và vitamin.

69.q: According to the writer, healing requires …
o: staying in hospital for a long time.
a lot of money and the best private hospital in the country.
only good surgery.
emotional resilience, support and the willingness to accept help.

69.q: Before the accident, the writer rarely visited a clinic.
69.e: Trước đó anh trẻ, khỏe và hiếm khi đi khám.

69.q: The surgeon did not mention any risks before the operation.
69.e: Bác sĩ có mô tả các rủi ro như nhiễm trùng hay tổn thương dây thần kinh.

69.q: The writer progressed from short walks to swimming.
69.e: Dần dần anh tiến tới đi bộ ngắn rồi bơi.

69.q: The writer has returned to the same gym.
69.e: Bài không nói anh có quay lại phòng gym đó không.

69.q: Have you or someone you know recovered from an illness or injury? What helped the most during recovery?
69.h: Kể ngắn gọn tình huống bằng thì quá khứ, nêu 2–3 yếu tố giúp hồi phục (What helped most was…) và bài học rút ra.

70.q: What made the climate crisis feel urgent and personal to the writer?
o: Seeing the destruction of the landscape where she grew up
A conversation with a scientist
A documentary she watched about melting ice at the North Pole
A lecture at university
70.e: Tận mắt thấy quê nhà bị tàn phá khiến khủng hoảng khí hậu trở nên cấp bách và mang tính cá nhân.

70.q: Why does the writer eat much less meat?
o: Meat is too expensive for her family, especially beef and pork.
Beef production generates a considerable amount of greenhouse gas.
Her doctor told her to.
She does not like the taste.

70.q: What is the writer's view of individual action?
o: It has limits; governments and businesses must also act.
It is completely useless.
It is enough to solve climate change if everyone does their part.
It is more important than politics.
70.e: Hành động cá nhân có giới hạn; quá trình chuyển đổi phụ thuộc phần lớn vào chính phủ và doanh nghiệp.

70.q: In paragraph 3, "despair does not help anyone" means …
o: feeling hopeless will not solve the problem.
everyone should feel sad.
people should not help each other with big problems.
the problem is not serious.
70.e: "despair" = tuyệt vọng; tác giả nhận ra tuyệt vọng không giúp được gì nên chuyển sang hành động.

70.q: Which statement best describes the writer's attitude at the end?
o: Hopeless
Angry and aggressive
Not interested
Worried but hopeful
70.e: Mối đe dọa đáng sợ, nhưng tác giả tin vẫn có thể đảm bảo một tương lai đáng sống.

70.q: A factory has replaced the forest near the writer's hometown.
70.e: Một nhà máy lớn đã thay thế khu rừng.

70.q: The solar panels have increased the family's energy bills.
70.e: Tấm pin mặt trời đã giảm hóa đơn năng lượng đáng kể.

70.q: The writer joined a group that restores forests and preserves wetlands.
70.e: Cô tham gia một sáng kiến bảo tồn phục hồi rừng và bảo vệ vùng đất ngập nước.

70.q: The writer works as a scientist studying climate change.
70.e: Bài nhắc đến các nhà khoa học nói chung, không nói tác giả làm nghề gì.

70.q: Should protecting the environment be mainly the job of individuals or of governments and businesses? Give your opinion with reasons.
70.h: Nêu quan điểm rõ ràng, đưa 2 lý do có ví dụ, và thừa nhận một ý của phía ngược lại (Of course, … However, …).

71.q: Why did the writer not care about politics before?
o: He thought nothing would change whoever was elected.
He was too young to vote.
He lived abroad.
He was too busy at work to read about politics or vote.
71.e: Anh cho rằng ai đắc cử thì cũng chẳng có gì thay đổi.

71.q: What did the local council propose?
o: Raising local taxes
Building a new school next to the library
Building more houses
Closing the public library to build a car park
71.e: Hội đồng đề xuất đóng thư viện công cộng để xây bãi đỗ xe đắt tiền.

71.q: What did the writer discover about democracy?
o: Demonstrations never work.
Ordinary people have more power than he thought, but only if they participate.
Ordinary people have no power, because politicians always do what they want.
Only politicians can change things.
71.e: Trong nền dân chủ, người dân thường có nhiều quyền lực hơn anh nghĩ, nhưng chỉ khi họ tham gia.

71.q: Which people does the writer NOT respect in debates?
o: People who promote racism or violence
People who vote differently
People who are older than him and have traditional views
People who disagree with him
71.e: Anh tôn trọng người có quan điểm đối lập, miễn là họ tranh luận trung thực và không cổ xúy phân biệt chủng tộc hay bạo lực.

71.q: What does the writer mean by "Democratic status is not guaranteed"?
o: Democracy is not important.
Only the government can protect democracy and the courts.
Democracy must be protected by citizens who pay attention.
Democracy will always exist, whatever citizens do.
71.e: Dân chủ không tự nhiên có mãi; nó phải được bảo vệ bởi những công dân chịu để tâm.

71.q: The library offered free courses for elderly residents.
71.e: Thư viện có các khóa học miễn phí cho người cao tuổi.

71.q: The library was closed despite the campaign.
71.e: Thị trưởng rút lại đề xuất và thư viện vẫn mở cửa.

71.q: The writer always agrees with his friends about political issues.
71.e: Anh không phải lúc nào cũng đồng ý với bạn bè.

71.q: The writer later became a member of the local council.
71.e: Bài không nói anh tham gia hội đồng địa phương.

71.q: Is there a local issue (in your school, city or community) that you care about? What could ordinary people do to change it?
71.h: Mô tả vấn đề, giải thích vì sao bạn quan tâm, và đề xuất 2–3 hành động cụ thể (People could… / We should…).

72.q: What is the writer's view of creativity?
o: It is a gift for a few geniuses who are born with special talent.
It is only useful for artists.
It cannot be learned.
It is a skill anyone can develop through practice.
72.e: Tác giả từng nghĩ sáng tạo là năng khiếu, nhưng giờ thấy đó là kỹ năng ai cũng rèn được.

72.q: How did the writer's creative journey begin?
o: With music
With writing a novel
With drawing humorous comics about her family
With painting lessons at a local art school
72.e: Thời thiếu niên cô vẽ truyện tranh hài về gia đình và đăng lên mạng.

72.q: According to the writer, what is the secret of creative work?
o: Only work when you are happy.
Show up and work every day, regardless of mood.
Wait for inspiration before you start any project.
Publish everything you make.
72.e: Bí quyết là không chờ cảm hứng mà làm việc mỗi ngày.

72.q: How does the writer deal with criticism now?
o: She separates useful feedback from simple negativity.
She ignores all comments.
She stops posting her work for a while after a bad review.
She replies angrily.
72.e: Cô phân biệt góp ý hữu ích với sự tiêu cực đơn thuần.

72.q: What does the writer suggest in the last paragraph?
o: You must produce something spectacular to call yourself creative.
You should study graphic design.
You should try to become famous.
You only need to make something and enjoy making it.
72.e: Không cần nổi tiếng hay tạo ra thứ ngoạn mục, chỉ cần làm ra một thứ gì đó.

72.q: The writer's early comic drafts were excellent.
72.e: Những bản nháp đầu tiên rất tệ.

72.q: The writer writes or draws for one hour each morning.
72.e: Mỗi sáng cô viết hoặc vẽ một tiếng.

72.q: Most of what the writer produces is published.
72.e: Phần lớn những gì cô làm ra không bao giờ được xuất bản.

72.q: The writer has won an award for her animation.
72.e: Bài không nhắc đến giải thưởng.

72.q: Choose a creative activity you would like to practise (writing, drawing, cooking, music…). How could you build a daily habit around it?
72.h: Nêu hoạt động, thời gian và địa điểm cụ thể (every morning for 20 minutes…), cách duy trì khi không có cảm hứng, và cách xử lý lời chê.

73.q: What was the writer's idea of travel before?
o: Backpacking around the world with friends
A package holiday at a beach resort
Visiting relatives
Business trips
73.e: Trước đây du lịch với anh là kỳ nghỉ trọn gói ở khu nghỉ dưỡng bãi biển.

73.q: How did the writer get to his guesthouse after landing?
o: By taxi on the highway to a downtown hotel
On foot
By train
By local bus through narrow lanes
73.e: Thay vì đi taxi, anh đi xe buýt địa phương.

73.q: Who explained the history of the colony?
o: A monk
A local historian
A guide from the hotel
A fisherman
73.e: Một nhà sử học địa phương giải thích về thuộc địa trên bờ biển.

o: With a paper map
With GPS on a phone
Using the stars and the wind
By following the cruise ship
73.e: Việc định hướng dựa vào sao và gió, không dựa vào điện thoại.

73.q: According to the writer, when do the best travel experiences happen?
o: When you are curious, open to strangers and willing to feel uncomfortable
When you follow the guidebook carefully and visit every famous place
When you travel in large groups
When you stay in luxury hotels
73.e: Trải nghiệm hay nhất hiếm khi có trong sách hướng dẫn.

73.q: The writer travelled for three months on a tight budget.
73.e: Năm 25 tuổi, anh đi ba tháng với ngân sách eo hẹp.

73.q: The writer bought a return ticket before leaving.
The writer was invited to a hill tribe ceremony.
73.e: Ở một ngôi làng xa xôi, anh được mời dự nghi lễ của một bộ tộc vùng đồi.

73.q: The writer wrote a guidebook after his journey.
73.e: Bài không nói anh viết sách hướng dẫn.

73.q: What is the difference between a "tourist" and a "traveller" for you? Describe a trip where you experienced a place more deeply.
73.h: Nêu định nghĩa của bạn, rồi kể một chuyến đi (thì quá khứ) với ít nhất một trải nghiệm "ngoài sách hướng dẫn".

74.q: What was the writer's thesis about?
o: Electronics
Artificial intelligence
Statistics
Climate change and the environment
74.e: Luận văn về trí tuệ nhân tạo.

74.q: What question from the supervisor changed everything?
o: When will you finish?
How do you know your results are valid and not just random?
Have you read enough books?
Why did you choose this topic instead of an easier one?
74.e: Câu hỏi của thầy hướng dẫn khiến tác giả xem lại cách đo lường.

o: The test data was too small and too similar to the training data.
The supervisor changed the results without telling him.
The computer was too slow to run the tests properly on time.
The code had no bugs.
74.e: Dữ liệu kiểm tra quá nhỏ và giống dữ liệu huấn luyện nên độ chính xác cao là ảo.

74.q: According to the writer, what is research really about?
o: Being precise and honest
Getting impressive results
Working alone
Proving yourself right
74.e: Nghiên cứu không phải để chứng minh mình đúng.

74.q: What does the writer's supervisor think a good researcher should achieve?
o: The highest possible accuracy on every single test
A published paper
Careful, transparent work that others can test and build on
Sophisticated claims
74.e: Không phải tuyên bố tinh vi mà là công việc cẩn thận, minh bạch.

74.q: At the beginning, the writer was confident about the thesis.
74.e: Ban đầu tác giả rất tự tin.

74.q: The writer kept all his original experiment without changes.
74.e: Anh phải xây lại toàn bộ thí nghiệm và xóa công sức nhiều tuần.

74.q: A classmate from the electronics department helped him interpret graphs.
74.e: Một bạn ở khoa điện tử giúp diễn giải biểu đồ.

74.q: The writer's final results were better than his original prediction.
74.e: Kết quả khiêm tốn hơn dự đoán ban đầu nhưng đáng tin cậy.

74.q: Have you ever worked on a project where your first results were wrong or misleading? What did you learn about doing careful work?
74.h: Kể ngắn gọn dự án bằng thì quá khứ (At first… / Then I realized that…), nêu bài học về tính chính xác và trung thực.

75.q: What does "I was a model pupil" mean?
o: She was a bad student.
She worked as a fashion model while she was studying.
She was a perfect student who followed all the rules.
She made models in class.
75.e: "model pupil" = học sinh gương mẫu; câu sau mô tả cô học thuộc, thi đỗ điểm cao.

75.q: What problem did the writer face in her first job?
o: Her manager was unfriendly.
She did not understand the technology that her company used.
There was no single correct answer and she had to think for herself.
She had too little work.
75.e: Ngoài đời thường không có một đáp án đúng duy nhất.

75.q: What did the writer do to "educate herself again"?
o: She went back to university full time to study philosophy.
She stopped working.
She hired a private tutor.
She read philosophy and psychology and joined workshops.
75.e: Cô đọc sách triết học, tâm lý học và tham gia workshop viết, nói.

75.q: How does the writer view formal education?
o: It should be replaced by work.
It is valuable but relatively narrow.
It is useless in real life.
It is the only real learning.
75.e: Giáo dục chính quy là phương tiện quý giá nhưng tương đối hẹp.

75.q: What is the writer's main advice?
o: Get as many degrees and certificates as possible.
Leave university early.
Treat your degree as the beginning of your education, not the end.
Only read academic books, because they are the most reliable sources.

75.q: When her manager asked her to evaluate a project, there was a clear guide to follow.
75.e: Không có sách giáo khoa, tài liệu hay tiêu chí rõ ràng.

75.q: The writer keeps a notebook about her own mistakes.
75.e: Cô giữ một cuốn sổ ghi những quan sát về lỗi của mình.

75.q: The writer's manager had studied philosophy.
75.e: Bài không nói gì về việc học của người quản lý.

75.q: What is one important skill that school did not teach you? How are you learning it now, or how could you learn it?
75.h: Nêu kỹ năng, một tình huống thực tế cho thấy bạn cần nó, và cách tự học (I am learning it by… / I could…).

76.q: Why did the writer start learning martial arts?
o: Because her parents were both national champions
To become famous
Because she was small and wanted to feel less vulnerable
To lose weight before a competition
76.e: Cô bắt đầu năm 15 tuổi vì nhỏ người và muốn bớt cảm giác dễ bị tổn thương.

76.q: According to the teacher, who is your real rival?
o: The person you were yesterday
The national champion
Your classmates
The referee
76.e: Đối thủ thật sự là chính mình của ngày hôm qua.

76.q: Why did the writer lose one match?
o: She was injured in the first minute of the fight.
She arrived late.
Her opponent was much bigger.
She ignored the referee's warning and received a penalty.
76.e: Vì quá khao khát thắng, cô phớt lờ cảnh cáo của trọng tài và bị phạt.

76.q: What lesson did the writer learn from writing a letter of apology?
o: Losing is not important.
Pride without self-control is dangerous.
Letters are better than words.
Referees are always unfair to young fighters.

76.q: How does the writer use her martial arts approach to fear in daily life?
o: She asks her teacher for help.
She always attacks problems quickly before they become bigger.
She avoids all difficult situations.
She pauses before reacting and chooses her battles wisely.
76.e: Cô dừng lại trước khi phản ứng, cân nhắc tình huống và chọn trận để đánh.

76.q: The writer's first lesson was mostly about falling over and getting up.
76.e: Buổi học đầu là ngã xuống rồi đứng dậy suốt một tiếng.

76.q: The writer won a gold medal in a regional championship.
An older student who had survived cancer became an outstanding fighter.
76.e: Một học viên lớn tuổi từng vượt qua ung thư trở thành võ sĩ xuất sắc.

76.q: The writer now teaches martial arts to children.
76.e: Bài không nói cô có dạy võ.

76.q: "Your real rival is the person you were yesterday." What does this mean to you? Describe one area of your life where you want to beat your "yesterday self".
76.h: Giải thích câu nói bằng lời của bạn, chọn một lĩnh vực cụ thể (học tập, sức khỏe…) và mô tả cách đo tiến bộ của chính mình.

77.q: How did the writer's parents meet?
o: At a friend's wedding
Through friends abroad
At university
As young workers in a factory
77.e: Bố mẹ gặp nhau khi là công nhân trẻ trong một nhà máy.

77.q: What happened when the mother was pregnant with the older sibling?
o: They won some money.
They moved abroad.
The father lost his job.
They bought a small house.
77.e: Khi mẹ mang thai, bố mất việc và họ sống chung một phòng với ông bà.

77.q: Which of these is one of the promises the parents made?
o: Never to spend money
Never to go to bed angry
Never to argue
Never to visit relatives
77.e: Họ hứa không bao giờ đi ngủ khi còn giận nhau.

77.q: What does the father mean by "Regret is a heavy load"?
o: You should never make mistakes.
Heavy things are hard to carry.
Regret helps you remember your mistakes so you do not repeat them.
Carrying old regrets for years is exhausting, so forgive.
77.e: Câu nói gắn với việc tha thứ, không ôm giữ cay đắng.

77.q: According to the writer, a lasting relationship is built through …
o: never arguing about anything
small daily acts of care, patience and respect
expensive gifts
luck and good fortune at the start

77.q: The parents' story was a perfect fairy-tale romance.
77.e: Câu chuyện của họ không phải chuyện cổ tích.

77.q: The mother once seriously thought about divorce.
77.e: Mẹ thừa nhận có lúc nghiêm túc nghĩ đến ly hôn.

77.q: The parents still enjoy walking together in the evening.
77.e: Họ vẫn thích đi dạo cùng nhau buổi tối.

77.q: The parents are very religious and go to church every week.
77.e: Họ không đặc biệt sùng đạo.

77.q: What do you think keeps a long friendship or relationship strong? Use an example from someone you know.
77.h: Nêu 2–3 yếu tố, minh họa bằng một cặp đôi hoặc tình bạn bạn biết (They always… / When…, they…).

78.q: What did the writer's company produce?
o: Clothing
Eco-friendly phone cases
Software
Mobile phones and chargers
78.e: Công ty sản xuất ốp điện thoại thân thiện với môi trường.

78.q: Which problem was NOT part of the company's collapse?
o: A recession
Rising inflation
A shortage of materials
A fire in the warehouse
78.e: Suy thoái, lạm phát và thiếu nguyên liệu đều được nhắc đến; hỏa hoạn thì không.

78.q: What was the founders' biggest mistake when things went wrong?
o: They hoped the market would recover instead of facing reality.
They sold the company too early.
They fired all their staff and tried to do everything themselves.
They stopped advertising.
78.e: Thay vì đối mặt với thực tế, họ đoán thị trường sẽ sớm phục hồi.

78.q: What did the business consultant say?
o: You need more investors.
Startups usually succeed if they have good investors.
You should never start a business.
Most startups fail; what matters is what you learn.
78.e: Lời của chuyên gia tư vấn.

78.q: How does the writer feel about starting a new business now?
o: He wants to work for others forever
He has no interest
Too frightened to try again after losing everything
Not frightened; he knows he can overcome obstacles
78.e: Viễn cảnh đó không còn làm anh sợ.

78.q: A local celebrity agreed to sponsor the company.
78.e: Một người nổi tiếng địa phương đồng ý tài trợ.

78.q: Revenue was lower than expected in the first six months.
78.e: Doanh thu vượt kỳ vọng trong sáu tháng đầu.

78.q: The negotiations with suppliers were successful.
The writer's university friend now works at the same large company.
78.e: Bài chỉ nói tác giả đang làm ở một công ty lớn; không nói về người bạn đồng sáng lập.

78.q: Do you agree that "failure is not the end of the story"? Describe a failure (yours or someone else's) that led to something better.
78.h: Nêu quan điểm, kể một thất bại cụ thể (thì quá khứ), và giải thích điều tốt đẹp hơn đến sau đó (As a result… / Later…).

79.q: Why did the grandmother finally tell her story?
o: A journalist interviewed her on television.
It was the anniversary of the tsunami.
She was writing a book about her life.
During a power cut, by candlelight, she decided to talk.
79.e: Một buổi tối mất điện, dưới ánh nến, bà cuối cùng đã kể.

79.q: What happened just before the wave came?
o: The water withdrew from the beach.
There was a big storm with strong winds.
Birds flew away.
The sky turned black.
79.e: Vài phút sau trận động đất, nước biển rút khỏi bãi một cách bất thường.

79.q: What was the grandmother's deepest wound?
o: Losing her house and her boat
Hunger
Losing her best friend
Being injured
79.e: Đói rất khủng khiếp, nhưng mất người bạn thân nhất là vết thương sâu nhất.

79.q: What happened between the neighbouring villages after the disaster?
o: They moved to the city together.
Former rivals united to share what they had.
They became rivals.
They built a wall.
